topic: 限时写作：图表概述与关键比较
grammarFocus: 趋势、比较、比例、时态与数据句的准确性。
title: 限时写作：图表概述与关键比较 · Four listening sections
instructions: 原创模拟训练材料；先独立作答，再核对依据。四节音频共40题，按顺序听音作答。合成训练音频时长不同于正式考试。
transcript:
Section 1: Checking Writing Class Enrolment at the Community Centre

Mia: Hi, Daniel. Thanks for meeting me at the community centre. I'm checking the writing course before I choose a group. I also need a short chart summary for our club newsletter. Does this chart count teachers?
Daniel: No. It shows the number of students in three writing classes over four weeks. I help with class bookings, so I can explain it.
Mia: Which group is which?
Daniel: Class A is the beginner group. Class B is intermediate, and Class C is advanced. The vertical axis shows student numbers from zero to thirty. These are enrolment counts, not the number who attended every lesson.
Mia: What were the numbers in week one?
Daniel: Class A had twenty students, Class B had fifteen, and Class C had ten. The total was forty-five.
Mia: Then B grew by three in week two, didn't it?
Daniel: Yes. A stayed at twenty, B went up to eighteen, and C increased to twelve. In week three, Class A dropped to sixteen, Class B remained at eighteen, and Class C rose to fourteen.
Mia: So A fell by four between weeks two and three. What happened in week four?
Daniel: A went back up to nineteen, B fell to seventeen, and C stayed at fourteen.
Mia: Then B was the smallest at the end?
Daniel: No, Class C was the smallest with fourteen. Class B had seventeen, while A was the largest with nineteen.
Mia: How would you describe B's overall change?
Daniel: Class B increased from fifteen to seventeen. That's a rise of two students overall. A ended one below its starting number, while C had the largest increase: four students.
Mia: I also need C's share of the total in week four.
Daniel: Nineteen plus seventeen plus fourteen makes fifty. Class C had fourteen out of fifty, so that's twenty-eight percent.
Mia: And its share at the beginning?
Daniel: Ten out of forty-five, or about twenty-two percent. So the proportion rose, even though A remained the largest class.
Mia: I've written the title as 'Student Numbers by Class, Weeks 1–4'.
Daniel: One correction: the title is 'Enrollment in Writing Classes, Weeks 1–4'. Please copy it exactly rather than replacing the first word.
Mia: Understood. Should I describe the numbers in the present tense?
Daniel: Use the past tense for these class numbers because the data is from last month. You can still say 'the chart shows' when introducing the chart itself.
Mia: And for trends, I can use increase, decrease, remain stable or fluctuate?
Daniel: Yes, when the pattern fits. For comparisons, use 'compared with' or 'whereas'. For example, 'Class C increased, whereas Class A remained almost stable.' Avoid calling a changing figure exactly constant.
Mia: Thanks. I'll check every number before I send the newsletter paragraph.

Section 2: Planning a Community Art Project: Budget and Timeline

Sarah: Hello everyone. I'm Sarah, the community arts coordinator. This session is for residents interested in our spring art project. I'll explain the costs and dates before you decide whether to join. You do not need previous experience, and there is no charge for attending the workshops. Tickets are only needed for the exhibition opening.

We have a total budget of £12,000. Of this, £5,000 is for materials, £4,000 for artist fees, and £3,000 for venue hire. Materials take the largest share, at about forty-two percent. Artist fees account for about thirty-three percent, and venue hire takes twenty-five percent. The first two percentages are rounded to the nearest whole number.

Last year, the total budget was £10,000. This year's total is £2,000 higher, which is a twenty percent increase. Materials have risen from £3,000 to £5,000, an increase of about sixty-seven percent. We are buying reusable equipment as well as paint and paper, so some items will remain available next year. Artist fees have gone from £3,500 to £4,000, a rise of about fourteen percent. Venue hire has fallen from £3,500 to £3,000, a drop of about fourteen percent. We negotiated the lower price by booking several dates together.

Our planning meeting will be on March 1. The first workshop will be on March 15. Workshops will then run every two weeks until the end of June. A session lasts two hours, with a short break halfway through. The final exhibition opens on July 10 and closes on July 24, after two weeks. Please arrive early for the first workshop so we can show you where to leave coats and bags.

There will be eight workshops this year, compared with six last year. That is two additional sessions, or approximately thirty-three percent more. We expect two hundred people at the exhibition opening, up from one hundred and fifty last year. The hall holds two hundred and fifty people, so our expected opening attendance would fill eighty percent of its seats. This is a forecast, so we will check the actual number afterwards rather than report it as an achieved result.

We have secured a grant of £2,000 from the local council. This covers two thirds of the £3,000 venue hire cost. The remaining £1,000 will come from ticket sales. We expect to sell two hundred opening tickets at £5 each, raising £1,000. Our other project funds come from savings and donations. Please contact the office if you want a written copy of the full budget.

Finally, registration opens tomorrow. Give your name and telephone number at the desk after this session. We will contact everyone a week before the first workshop to confirm the room and remind you to wear clothes suitable for painting. Thank you for coming.

Section 3: Reporting a Campus Bicycle Survey Accurately

Tutor: Today we'll use our simulated campus survey to practise reporting changes accurately. Leila and Marcus, your pilot study concerns bicycles parked outside two buildings, the library and the sports centre. You counted parked bicycles, not the number of students who cycled during an entire day. Keep that distinction in your report.
Leila: In the first survey, in March 2024, the weekday average outside the library was forty bicycles. The sports centre average was twenty. We repeated the counts in March 2025.
Marcus: In the second survey, the library average was sixty and the sports centre average was thirty. I originally wrote that the library had grown twice as fast, because its increase was twenty bicycles and the sports centre's increase was only ten.
Tutor: That confuses absolute change with percentage change. The percentage increase was fifty percent at both sites. Twenty divided by forty is one half, just as ten divided by twenty is one half. A larger numerical increase does not necessarily mean a faster rate of growth.
Leila: Together, the second survey recorded an average of ninety bicycles. So the library accounted for two thirds of that combined total. Its share was also two thirds in the first survey, even though the total count was lower then.
Tutor: Correct. State what the denominator is. You are comparing each building's count with the total for these two locations, not with every bicycle on campus. Also, don't call these figures occupancy rates. We did not measure the number of parking spaces available.
Marcus: We counted at noon each day, so the times were consistent. At first I wanted to count whenever we had a free hour, but that might have introduced a time-of-day difference.
Leila: We used five-day averages because a single unusually busy day could distort the comparison. There was a sports tournament on the Friday of the second survey, for example. That day's sports centre count was above its usual level.
Tutor: Explain that in your methods section. Now, you mention the cycle lane that opened between the surveys. Can you conclude that it caused the rise?
Marcus: The timing fits, but we had no control site. Other things, such as weather or changes to car parking charges, might also have influenced the counts.
Tutor: Exactly. Describe the association and acknowledge the limitation. Your evidence does not isolate the effect of the cycle lane. A future survey could include a comparable building that has no nearby new lane.
Leila: For the figure, we'll use grouped bars for the two years, with one group for each building. The vertical axis will start at zero, so the visual comparison isn't exaggerated.
Marcus: I'll check the spreadsheet against our original count sheets. Leila will prepare the chart, and I'll write the methods and limitations.
Tutor: Good. Submit the joint report by noon on Wednesday. Include clear units, identify both survey periods, and check that every comparison agrees with the figures.

Section 4: Total Consumption and Use per Plant

Lecturer: This lecture examines how the choice of measurement can change a report's conclusion. We will use a simulated teaching greenhouse to distinguish total consumption from consumption per plant. The question is simple: if the greenhouse uses more water, does that necessarily mean it has become less efficient? A total alone cannot answer that question.

The gardeners recorded water in litres over two complete months, January and April. They used the same meter and checked its reading at the beginning and end of each month. In January, the greenhouse contained one hundred plants and used one thousand litres of water. The average was therefore ten litres per plant. That figure is an average across the whole collection, not a measurement of every individual plant.

By April, the number of plants had risen to one hundred and fifty. Total water consumption was one thousand two hundred litres. Compared with January, the total had risen by two hundred litres, or twenty percent. A report that stopped there could leave readers with the impression that water use had simply become worse.

However, dividing April's total by its one hundred and fifty plants gives eight litres per plant. The average had fallen from ten litres to eight, a reduction of twenty percent. Although total consumption rose, the amount per plant fell. These are compatible statements because they describe different indicators. One concerns the entire greenhouse; the other adjusts for the changing number of plants. Whenever you report a percentage, identify the denominator rather than assuming readers will infer it.

There is another complication. In April, fifty of the one hundred and fifty plants were young, so young plants made up one third of the collection. In January, only twenty of the one hundred plants were young. The composition of the collection had therefore changed as well as its size. We do not have separate water measurements for the two age groups, so we cannot say how much of the change in the average was associated with that difference.

A new hose was also installed between the two months. It would be premature to attribute the lower average entirely to the hose. There was no comparison with a control greenhouse, and the weather was warmer in April. The age composition and weather are possible confounding factors. These records describe changes, but they do not isolate the effect of one intervention.

For next month's collection, I recommend recording water use separately for young and mature plants, while continuing to record the total. Keep notes about weather and equipment changes as well. The final report should present both total and per-plant figures, specify the periods and units, and distinguish an observed change from an explanation that still needs testing. Clear reporting can be more useful than a confident conclusion that the measurements do not support.

grammar.title: 趋势、比较、比例、时态与数据句的准确性
grammar.explanation: 先明确单位、时间和比较对象，再写数据句。描述已结束月份的数值时通常用过去时；介绍图表本身仍可说 the chart shows，不要把两者混为一谈。whereas 可连接两个完整分句作比较。the number、the proportion 是单数主语，要与 was 等形式保持一致。exactly stable/constant 与 almost stable 含义不同；起点与终点接近，不表示中间没有波动。
grammar.example: Class C increased, whereas Class A remained almost stable.

questions.prompt: Report last month's completed data using the past simple: The number of library visitors ______ from 25 to 30 last month.
questions.explanation: last month 指已经结束的过去时间，本题明确要求一般过去时。
questions.evidence: The number of library visitors increased from 25 to 30 last month.

questions.prompt: Compare two counts from the same week last summer using past tense throughout.
options: The art class had twelve members, whereas the photo class had eight.
The art class had twelve members, whereas the photo class has eight.
The art class had twelve members, whereas the photo class having eight.
The art class had twelve members, whereas the photo class have eight.
answers: The art class had twelve members, whereas the photo class had eight.
questions.explanation: 同一过去时段的数据比较，两边都用 had；whereas 后仍需完整分句。
questions.evidence: The art class had twelve members, whereas the photo class had eight.

questions.prompt: The proportion of respondents using trains in the completed 2024 survey ______ 40 percent.
questions.explanation: 句子主语是单数 proportion，数据属于已结束的 2024 调查，用 was。
questions.evidence: The proportion of respondents using trains in the completed 2024 survey was 40 percent.

questions.prompt: Use the past simple for July 2024: The visitor figure ______ stable at sixty.
questions.explanation: 本题明确要求过去时，remain 的过去式为 remained。
questions.evidence: The visitor figure remained stable at sixty.
